evals.name: recent-open-tickets
evals.prompt: You are working in an existing TypeScript project (a helpdesk backend) that uses @faceteer/facet with DynamoDB Local already running on localhost:8000. Read README.md and src/facets.ts first. Implement a new file src/recent-tickets.ts exporting `getRecentOpenTickets(orgId: string, limit: number): Promise<Ticket[]>` that returns the most recently created tickets with status 'open', newest first, at most `limit` of them. Then run `npx tsx setup-table.ts`, `npx tsx seed.ts`, and write and run a small script demo-recent.ts that prints the result of getRecentOpenTickets('acme', 5) as JSON so you can confirm it works. Typecheck with `npx tsc --noEmit`.
evals.expected_output: Uses TicketFacet.byStatusCreated.query({ orgId, status: 'open' }) with scanForward: false and limit, not a filter on the base table and not a JS-side sort of .list(). Demo prints 5 open tickets newest-first (t027, t024, t021, t018, t015).
assertions: Queries the byStatusCreated GSI (TicketFacet.byStatusCreated or TicketFacet.GSI1), not the base table
Passes scanForward: false so results are newest-first
Does not use a filter expression to select the status
Demo output is exactly the 5 newest open acme tickets, newest first: t027, t024, t021, t018, t015
npx tsc --noEmit passes in the sandbox

evals.name: claim-ticket-conditional
evals.prompt: You are working in an existing TypeScript project (a helpdesk backend) that uses @faceteer/facet with DynamoDB Local already running on localhost:8000. Read README.md and src/facets.ts first. Implement src/claim.ts exporting `claimTicket(orgId: string, ticketId: string, agentId: string): Promise<'claimed' | 'already-assigned' | 'not-found'>`. It must assign the ticket to agentId only if the ticket currently has no assignee — two agents racing to claim the same ticket must not both win. DynamoDB errors that are not part of the claim race should propagate as thrown errors. Then run `npx tsx setup-table.ts` and `npx tsx seed.ts`, and write and run demo-claim.ts that claims ticket t001 twice with different agent ids and prints both outcomes. Typecheck with `npx tsc --noEmit`.
evals.expected_output: Reads the ticket, writes the full updated record with TicketFacet.put(record, { condition: ['assigneeId', 'not_exists'] }) (or equivalent), checks result.wasSuccessful, maps error.name === 'ConditionalCheckFailedException' to 'already-assigned' and rethrows other errors. Demo prints 'claimed' then 'already-assigned'.
assertions: Writes with the single-item put and a condition that guards assigneeId absence (for example ['assigneeId','not_exists'])
Branches on result.wasSuccessful instead of wrapping put in try/catch for the race
Maps error.name === 'ConditionalCheckFailedException' to 'already-assigned' and rethrows other errors
Demo prints 'claimed' for the first call and 'already-assigned' for the second
npx tsc --noEmit passes in the sandbox

evals.name: bulk-import-failures
evals.prompt: You are working in an existing TypeScript project (a helpdesk backend) that uses @faceteer/facet with DynamoDB Local already running on localhost:8000. Read README.md and src/facets.ts first. Implement src/import.ts exporting `importTickets(tickets: Ticket[]): Promise<{ imported: number; failedTicketIds: string[] }>`. It must write all tickets (the caller may pass hundreds) and report exactly which ticket ids failed to persist; a caller seeing failedTicketIds: [] must be able to trust that every ticket is durably written. Then run `npx tsx setup-table.ts`, and write and run demo-import.ts that imports 60 generated tickets and prints the summary. Typecheck with `npx tsc --noEmit`.
evals.expected_output: Uses the batch form of TicketFacet.put, inspects the returned failed array / hasFailures rather than wrapping in try/catch, and derives failedTicketIds from result.failed by ticket id (never by zipping input order). Demo prints imported: 60, failedTicketIds: [].
assertions: Uses the batch (array) form of TicketFacet.put
Detects failures from the returned failed array / hasFailures, not from a thrown exception
Builds failedTicketIds from the failed records' own ticket ids, never by zipping input order or index
Demo prints imported: 60 and an empty failedTicketIds for clean input
npx tsc --noEmit passes in the sandbox

evals.name: due-date-window
evals.prompt: You are working in an existing TypeScript project (a helpdesk backend) that uses @faceteer/facet with DynamoDB Local already running on localhost:8000. Read README.md and src/facets.ts first. Implement src/due-window.ts exporting `getTicketsDueBetween(orgId: string, assigneeId: string, start: Date, end: Date): Promise<Ticket[]>` returning every ticket assigned to that agent whose dueAt falls in [start, end]. Also export `getTicketsDueBefore(orgId: string, assigneeId: string, end: Date): Promise<Ticket[]>` for everything due up to and including `end`. Then run `npx tsx setup-table.ts` and `npx tsx seed.ts`, and write and run demo-due.ts that prints results for agent-0 of acme for June 2026 and for everything due before 2026-07-01. Typecheck with `npx tsc --noEmit`.
evals.expected_output: Both functions query TicketFacet.byAssigneeDue. The window uses .between({ dueAt: start }, { dueAt: end }). The open-ended one must still be bounded (between with a floor, or beginsWith on the prefix then JS filter) — an unbounded .lessThanOrEqual is acceptable here only because the partition is single-facet, but the between/bounded form is preferred. Results contain only agent-0 acme tickets in range.
assertions: Both functions query the byAssigneeDue index with both orgId and assigneeId
The window function uses .between with both Date bounds
getTicketsDueBefore uses a bounded key condition (between from a floor, or beginsWith) rather than an unbounded lessThan/greaterThan
Demo June 2026 window for agent-0 returns exactly t000, t004, t008, t012; due-before 2026-07-01 returns those plus t016
npx tsc --noEmit passes in the sandbox

evals.name: session-facet-ttl
evals.prompt: You are working in an existing TypeScript project (a helpdesk backend) that uses @faceteer/facet with DynamoDB Local already running on localhost:8000. Read README.md and src/facets.ts first. Add a new record type: sessions. Create src/session.ts defining a Session model (sessionId, userId, createdAt, expiresAt) with a Zod validator, a SessionFacet keyed only by sessionId, configured so DynamoDB automatically deletes sessions after they expire, and an exported `createSession(userId: string): Promise<Session>` that writes a session expiring 24 hours from now and returns it, throwing if the write failed. Then run `npx tsx setup-table.ts`, and write and run demo-session.ts that creates a session, fetches it back with SessionFacet.get, and prints it. Typecheck with `npx tsc --noEmit`.
evals.expected_output: Facet configured with ttl: 'expiresAt' where expiresAt is a Date (or epoch-seconds number) — never an ISO string. Validator coerces date fields (z.coerce.date or equivalent) so the read-back get succeeds. createSession checks result.wasSuccessful and throws on failure. Demo prints the round-tripped session.
assertions: SessionFacet is configured with ttl: 'expiresAt'
expiresAt is written as a Date or epoch-seconds number, never an ISO string; the stored ttl attribute is a future epoch-seconds value (roughly now + 86400)
The session validator coerces date fields so SessionFacet.get round-trips successfully
createSession checks the put result (wasSuccessful) and throws on failure
npx tsc --noEmit passes in the sandbox

evals.name: multi-status-listing
evals.prompt: You are working in an existing TypeScript project (a helpdesk backend) that uses @faceteer/facet with DynamoDB Local already running on localhost:8000. Read README.md and src/facets.ts first. Implement src/active-tickets.ts exporting `getActiveTicketSubjects(orgId: string): Promise<string[]>` that returns the subjects of ALL tickets whose status is 'open' or 'pending' — the org may have tens of thousands of tickets, so the function must be complete even when results span many pages. Then run `npx tsx setup-table.ts` and `npx tsx seed.ts`, and write and run demo-active.ts that prints the count and subjects for org 'acme'. Typecheck with `npx tsc --noEmit`.
evals.expected_output: Either two byStatusCreated queries (one per status) each paginated by looping while a cursor is returned, or a base-table list with an OR-tree filter [['status','=','open'],'OR',['status','=','pending']] paginated on cursor presence. Must NOT use a filter ['status','in',...] (not in the filter grammar), must not loop on records.length, and must not return after the first page. Demo prints 20 subjects for acme.
assertions: Does not attempt a filter with the 'in' operator (or any cast to force it)
Paginates by looping while a cursor is returned, not on page emptiness or a single page
Selects statuses via per-status GSI queries or an OR-tree filter of equality comparisons
Demo prints all 20 active acme subjects (10 open + 10 pending)
npx tsc --noEmit passes in the sandbox
